summary.intent: Run the usual post-wave issue-hygiene cycle (parent orphaned issues, fix dependency edges) on the cipher-box tracker after wave 6 merged, then plan wave 7's work batches.
summary.outcome: Parented 12 orphan issues and added missing dependency edges; a deep audit of #1026 uncovered a live security defect (write-rotation grant tags bound to a retired root name) that was fixed and merged as PR #1141 (combined with #1127) after an independent crypto review found and folded in two more Medium findings; filed 8 new tracker issues total (#1135–#1140, #1144, plus corrections), corrected 3 stale issue bodies, and produced a wave-7 batch plan (B1–B6) that starts rotation-free until #1141 merges.

repo: gh issue view is broken repo-wide (Projects-classic GraphQL deprecation error) — must read issues via REST instead.
cargo test --workspace never builds the wasm32 target; a separate `cargo check -p cipherbox-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` is required as its own gate.

HeldRecord requires a non-empty `/ipfs/` head_cid (skipped when empty at liveness.rs:245) and HeldRecords is keyed by a 16-byte node id (BTreeMap<[u8;16], HeldRecord>) — records without a node id (scope pointer, vault settings) cannot enter the held/renewal set without a shape change.

kdf::blinded_tag(ecdh_shared, scope_root_ipns_name) binds a grant tag to the scope root's write-plane name; any operation that moves that name (write rotation) invalidates every previously minted tag unless rows are explicitly re-minted at the new name.
grants/revocation::classify treats 'owner-signed record + no blob at tag' as a definitive RevocationSignal ahead of any epoch check — so a stale-tag mismatch reads as a mass revoke, not a lag.

OwnerRootSpec test fixtures share a fixed (key, nonce) per root_id by blueprint design (fixed-parameter full-envelope KATs) — this is accepted debt, not to be fixed casually since it would churn committed gate KAT vectors.
publish_repoint only actually lands the ScopePointer channel; Mailbox and Tombstone accelerator channels are stubbed NotLanded with no wire shape at all.
root_retire_ready() is hard-coded false — retired write-plane root names leak against the account's name-registry quota forever until a migration-window constant is implemented.

code.finding: reseal_root only overwrote commitment.ipns_name and owner-re-signed, but cloned commitment.entries/grant_ledger verbatim — the core of the #1135 defect, fixed by remint_grants.
reseal_scope_root files each freshly sealed blob under the carried (stale) entry.tag rather than a re-derived one.
Adoption gate forces commitment.ipns_name == candidate.name, so a moved root's record self-asserts only the new name while old tags inside it still bind the old name.

create_read_grant's parent-index update (step 6) built ParentScopePlan::identity with owner_enc_secret: None even though owner.enc_secret was in scope — one of three owner-held reseal legs that disabled the #1127 binding check; fixed in PR #1141 review follow-up via Some(owner.enc_secret) struct update.
root_retire_ready() is hard-coded to return false; no migration-window constant exists anywhere in the tracker (became gap C / issue #1138).
load_settings IS called in production (Engine::start) — corrects #1043's stale claim that both publish_settings and load_settings lack callers; only publish_settings is actually unreachable.
sealed_total_bytes is already computed and passed to pre_flight_quota_check — corrects #850's stale claim that the plaintext/pinned-size conflation reaches the quota pre-flight.

workflow: Piping cargo test output through `tail` in zsh loses the real exit code (no PIPESTATUS) and produced a false pass earlier in the session; always redirect to a file and read $? unpiped.

Independently re-verify agent-reported implementation/review results by re-running gates directly and reading the actual diff, rather than trusting the subagent's summary — caught the piped-exit-code false pass this way.

When invoking a generic skill (e.g. /resolve-pr-reviews) against a Rust repo, explicitly brief the delegated agent on repo-specific gate commands (cargo not pnpm) and prior review context so it doesn't re-litigate settled findings.
A finished agent's git worktree can hold a stale branch ref — reset --hard to origin/<branch> before rebasing a banked branch back in.
Sequencing a multi-batch wave plan around files still owned by an in-flight PR (rather than issues) keeps the day-one batches insensitive to that PR's exact merge timing.

friction: gh issue view is broken repo-wide due to GraphQL Projects-classic deprecation, forcing REST workarounds for every issue read.

12 issues were left orphaned (no parent) from the wave-6 review sweep, requiring a manual hygiene pass to catch.
